study type: Cross-sectional comparative study with prospective facility-based follow-up
cohort: Pregnant women in their third trimester divided into two groups: 51 with oligohydramnios and 102 without oligohydramnios
finding: Oligohydramnios was significantly associated with increased cesarean delivery rates, lower five-minute Apgar scores, and higher NICU admission rates.
birth_weight: Measured, but no significant difference found between groups
